output.brief:
The August drop came almost entirely from floors 6-8. Their cooling chiller failed on 4 August and wasn't repaired until 19 August. Rooms ran 26-29 C, and the room comfort score on those floors fell from 8.4 to 6.1. Scores for 5-20 August checkouts on those floors were 6.8, then recovered to 8.4 once cooling was restored. All 56 heat complaints came from floors 6-8. Floors 1-5 barely moved.

Cleanliness scores, inspection pass rates and housekeeping complaints are flat, so there's no evidence against Orrin. Kiosk use, queue times and check-in scores are also flat. The survey method didn't change.

The 6% rate rise is unresolved. Value scores dip every August, and this year's dip on floors 1-5 is only slightly larger.

I'd not serve notice on Orrin, not pull the kiosks, and not exclude the floor 6-8 responses. I'd reinstate the deferred chiller maintenance on both chillers, stock critical spare parts, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. A follow-up offer to the affected guests is reasonable, since they already got an apology and credit. Hold off on reversing the rate rise and watch value scores. I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis. I didn't collect any extra evidence.
